KS-T00.statement: Finite object/relation space is well-formed: unique ids, incident atoms exist, registered types, non-negative weights and resources.

KS-T01.statement: Antichain profiles with ⊕ (alternative) and ⊗ (conjunctive) form a commutative idempotent semiring with 0 = ∅, 1 = {∅}.

KS-T21.statement: Three-valued liveness on warrant intervals (lower = exhibited, upper = possible) is an exact homomorphism from (⊕, ⊗) to Kleene strong (∨, ∧); certified profiles reduce to two-valued ℓ_R; refinement is monotone (UNKNOWN → LIVE|DEAD only).

KS-T02.statement: Revocation of any required tail or of the edge disables conjunctive firing for every activation vector; with three-valued liveness the verdict is ENABLED/DISABLED/UNKNOWN.

KS-T03.statement: The warranted navigation matrix is substochastic.

KS-T04.statement: Gate-based exact-share revocation equals pruning with the original pre-revocation denominators (matrix level).

KS-T04b.statement: Exact-share retraction propagates to the fixed point: (i) revoked atoms have zero activation, (ii) atoms outside Reach(dead) are exactly unchanged, (iii) activation is monotone non-increasing, (iv) reinstatement restores the pre-revocation vector exactly.

KS-T04c.statement: Prune–solve equivalence at the fixed point and at the reacting subgraph: Solve_warranted(K, R, q) = Solve_warranted(Prune_R(K), ∅, q) under identical normalisation.

KS-T05.statement: Restart navigation a ← α s + (1−α) Pᵀ a is an ℓ1 contraction with a unique fixed point; iteration converges geometrically.

KS-T06.statement: Reaction surprise is zero for an atom whose query activation equals its background activation; a universal hub has zero surprise under a query-independent seed.

KS-T06b.statement: Two-direction hub theorem: a query touching hub and specific atom ranks the specific atom first by surprise while the hub is first by popularity; a hub-only query ranks the hub first by both.

KS-T07.statement: Quotient navigation commutes with pushforward iff the partition is Kemeny–Snell lumpable.

KS-T07b.statement: A representation move is admissible only under navigation lumpability ∧ warrant measurability (identical three-valued liveness within each block under every registered revocation).

KS-T08.statement: Every newly admitted live non-quarantined atom is incident to at least one live typed relation (semantic connectivity or quarantine).

KS-T09.statement: The dependency impact cone is the least dependency-closed superset of the changed set; cycles are handled by the fixed point.

KS-T22.statement: Reopening locality: after a revocation delta the forced reopening set is cone ∩ liveness-changed; cone members whose liveness is unchanged (alternative live warrant) need re-check only; activation outside Reach(dead) is exactly unchanged; unrelated evidence revocation is a no-op.

KS-T10a.statement: Translator invariance reduces to seed equality: equal seed vectors yield identical extraction.

KS-T11a.statement: The reacting subgraph is well-defined and unique; the prize-collecting optimiser is a distinct object whose optima may tie.

KS-T12.statement: Lifecycle-safe consolidation: a macro can be maintained/reopened in work proportional to the affected dependency region — CLAUSE (theory batch 7 G5): holds for query sets Q ⊆ exports of the consolidated region (gain (k−1)[t∈Q] − 2|Q∩internals|); the unconditional form is refuted (k = 1, Q = {x1}: 1 → 3).

KS-T23.statement: No authority from abstraction: Λ(summary) = Λ_corr ⊗ ⊗ Λ(exported); LIVE(summary) ⇒ live support exists below; DEAD/UNKNOWN propagate by KS-T21; authority is the meet and scope the intersection; a summary answers a query family only under a registered sufficiency certificate, else REFINE_REQUIRED.

KS-T17.statement: Stem-cell growth invariant: the loop acquire → compose → revoke → reinstate preserves KS-S1…S7, keeps the genome digest unchanged, and reaches a fixed point when nothing new can be acquired.

KS-T18.statement: Feedback cannot warrant: a FEEDBACK-admitted atom carries the certified-zero interval and is never LIVE, hence never enables firing; an EXACT_CHECKER atom enters with exact warrant.

KS-T19.statement: Navigation outcome is four-valued (FOUND / GAP_NOT_FOUND / OBSTRUCTION_WITNESSED / CANNOT_CHECK), exhaustive and exclusive; an obstruction is witnessed only when the ungated ceiling walker also fails; timeout alone is a gap; a zero budget is CANNOT_CHECK.

KS-T20.statement: Composition warrant is ⊗ (never ⊕); authority is the meet; scope the intersection — no amplification.

KS-T24.statement: Navigation is not truth: with every warrant certified-zero and identical weights, no atom is LIVE, warranted extraction is empty, and no edge is enabled, while exploratory activation is unchanged.

KS-A2.statement: A conjunctive hyperrelation is not equivalent to its pairwise expansion (enabling and navigation differ); pairwise reading requires an explicit certificate.

KS-A1.statement: A new object type can be registered without changing warrant/navigation code.

KS-R1.statement: Every reference mechanic reports a non-compensatory resource vector; vectors are compared by Pareto dominance, never a scalar.

KS-P1.statement: No single parent among eight owns label-gated activation with exact-share retraction; the KSO law equals the two-parent product (JTMS/ATMS gate ∘ frozen-denominator spreading activation) — PARENT_PRODUCT_OWNED.

KS-EQ.statement: Old-vs-new equivalence: the canonical package reproduces the frozen reference on every registered witness (matrices, fixed points, navigate outcomes, retraction report, F-check outcomes) and on seeded random spaces.

KS-T51.statement: Lexical acquisition by exact alignment: one unknown token ↔ one meaning node no known lexeme accounts for; the new sense's warrant is exactly the demonstration's evidence; a second aligned concept adds a sense to the ambiguity set; revoking one sense's evidence kills that sense only; relearning yields a new record with lineage.

KS-T52.statement: Morphology induction over a registered suffix-rewrite class: a pure rule is CONTRADICTED by irregular pairs; HYBRID keeps the rule (⊗ of the covered pairs) plus exception rules (each pair's evidence) under the override law; exceptions beyond a registered fraction trigger SPLIT_RECOMMENDED; ablaut outside the class stays an exception (recorded class limit).

KS-T53.statement: Raw-corpus form induction yields UNGROUNDED_FORM_ONLY hypotheses with corpus authority and no world_truth/meaning coordinate; the interpreter never consults them; grounding requires aligned/grounded evidence (bind) — frequency never grounds; semantic gain of E2 alone is exactly zero.

KS-T54.statement: Grounded interaction: outcome observations of a registered outcome function eliminate hypotheses in the version space and warrant the object with those observations; an unregistered outcome is refused; success bits are FEEDBACK and never admit an object (KS-T18).

KS-T55.statement: Active learning: actions are chosen by expected elimination per unit cost over the version space (uniform prior); the gold-label action is prohibited; a singleton version space acts no further; hindsight regret is reported.

KS-T56.statement: Transfer is a registered scope move: meaning structures transfer across languages; lexemes, morphology and word order are language-scoped; senses are domain-scoped; style is not grammar; counter-evidence in the target scope refuses; the SOV mini-language under the English inventory yields UNKNOWN_CONSTRUCTION (detected, not forced) and its order is learned from demonstrations with meaning graphs intact.

KS-T57.statement: Retention protocol: after every episode the vector (new gain, old loss, unrelated change, reopened objects, update work) is reported with denominators; old loss after the E1 episode is 0/22.

KS-T58.statement: Regimes measured separately with disclosed information: E0 explicit lessons, E1 aligned demonstrations (with leakage-checked teacher examples), E2 raw corpus, E3 grounded interaction, E4 fixed curricula; no aggregate replaces the vector.

KS-T59.statement: BabyLM sample-efficiency programme, CHILDES adapters, matched comparator curves — custody manifests only (Gutenberg acquired; BabyLM CANNOT_CHECK_BABYLM_DATA).

KS-T60.statement: Knowledge provenance: 'source asserts P' (IMPORTED, source=1), 'P parsed' (digest) and 'P verified' (separate evidence, verified=1) are distinct records; the fact warrant is ⊕ assertions ⊗ verification; repetition of assertions never raises authority; revoking one source kills exactly the facts it alone supported.

KS-T61.statement: Realisation is a codec: every candidate surface is re-interpreted and kept only if its canonical digest equals the intended meaning; style (passive preference, contractions, certified pronouns) selects among checked variants and never changes meaning; a paraphrase that drops negation fails the reverse reading.

KS-T62.statement: ResponsePlan.v1 sits above realisation; content is selected only from live world facts and speaker commitments; unverified claims carry REPORTED, unknowns REPORT_UNKNOWN, contradictions REPORT_UNCERTAIN; a missing intermediate premise in an explanation is a feedback event naming the gap; the planner cannot mint a premise (the mutant does).

KS-T43.statement: Three-layer separation: speaker commitments are OBSERVATION evidence with speaker authority and conversation scope; the machine layer changes only by propose_promote under a LIVE bridge with the authority meet; ten speakers' agreement leaves the machine layer empty.

KS-T44.statement: Correction is supersession: the new commitment's evidence supersedes the old, the old evidence is revoked (KS-T22 reopens exactly the dependents), both records are linked, history is never edited; unrelated commitments are untouched; retraction revokes without a successor.

KS-T45.statement: Reference is four-valued from constraints; recency and mention count order an ambiguity set only; an unconstrained referent is UNKNOWN_REFERENT, never the nearest string.

KS-T46.statement: Clarification value = expected number of registered query cells determined after the answer (uniform prior over the ambiguity set) − cost − repeat penalty; irrelevant ambiguity has value 0 (no question); a question pinning every candidate dominates one isolating a single candidate under matched cost; repeats have non-positive value; the answer is INTERACTION evidence and never a score collapse.

KS-T47.statement: External commitment gate: a surface commits iff its meaning digest equals the plan's, every asserted proposition is LIVE (or REPORTED when resting on speaker commitments), the epistemic marker equals the state's required marker, referents are resolved, no protected content id appears, and the renderer held no store handle; refusals are structured feedback events naming the stage to reopen.

KS-T48.statement: Contradictory commitments (p and ¬p) are both kept; a question on p is answered REPORT_UNCERTAIN citing both; majority never resolves; resolution only by supersession, retraction or a bridge.

KS-T49.statement: Persistence: the workspace is written atomically after every mutation and reloaded on resume with the runtime ledger; a reference to evidence absent from the ledger is CANNOT_CHECK; a midway restart changes no behaviour.

KS-T50.statement: Real-conversation evaluation (MultiWOZ 2.4 comparator, protected human conversations) — custody script provided; results are M4 follow-ups.

KS-T34.statement: Canonical meaning form: for typed hypergraph fragments with ≤ 7 nodes, canonical(g1) = canonical(g2) iff g1 ≅ g2 (exhaustive within colour classes); beyond the bound CANNOT_CHECK, never a hash; seed = seed ∘ can so two parsers with different node numbering seed navigation identically.

KS-T35.statement: Lexical ambiguity is an ambiguity set: a token's readings are candidates each with its own interval; the token is READINGS iff exactly one LIVE and none UNKNOWN, AMBIGUOUS otherwise; collapse only by revocation/clarification evidence; same-analysis derivations merge as ⊕; unknown tokens are UNKNOWN_LEXEME (no spelling-similarity guess).

KS-T36.statement: Morphological override law: a LIVE EXCEPTION rule for (lemma, category, features) pre-empts every PRODUCTIVE rule for that key whatever token is analysed; revoking the exception's evidence makes the regularised form available and touches no other lemma.

KS-T37.statement: Candidate warrant of a parse: Λ(candidate) = Λ(construction) ⊗ ⨂ Λ(parts), a phrase contributing its own ⊗; isomorphic candidates from different derivations merge as ⊕; the verdict is INTERPRETED iff exactly one LIVE candidate and none UNKNOWN; AMBIGUOUS retains all candidates and a score outside the lattice may only order them.

KS-T38.statement: Grounding boundary: parsing success yields said(speaker, meaning) as OBSERVATION evidence with Authority.of(speaker=1); world_truth is 0 and stays 0 under any composition of speakers; answers cite evidence and return UNKNOWN when nothing on record supports or denies; contradictory statements are both kept; the only promotion is the authority meet with a bridge.

KS-T39.statement: Construction acquisition: over a registered finite pattern class, a demonstration (utterance, meaning) is consistent with h iff parsing under h realises an isomorphic meaning; promotion iff agreement on the query family; warrant = ⊗ of the pinning demonstrations; AMBIGUOUS is not promoted; CONTRADICTION is preserved; an instruction names a hypothesis and is refuted by a contradicting demonstration; constructions are language-scoped.

KS-T40.statement: Recursive composition: phrase-level constructions (produces=NP) are built bottom-up over spans and bound as single arguments by clause constructions; the merged fragment relabels the phrase head onto the argument node and keeps the phrase's ⊗ warrant.

KS-T41.statement: Freeze-before-outcome for evaluation: the protected split is fixed by content hash before tuning; held-out lexemes never appear in dev; the evaluation receipt is deleted before each run and its exit code checked (stale receipts are CANNOT_CHECK, ledger S14).

KS-T42.statement: Real-language evaluation (UD EWT structural, BLiMP acceptability comparator) — custody manifests bound; evaluators and results are M3 follow-ups.

KS-T104.statement: One runtime identity across the lifetime: the ledger root is constant and every component (chat, science ledger, self-model, work warrants) points at the same runtime at every phase boundary; a restart reopens the same ledger.

KS-T107.statement: Revision inside a lifetime: revoking a knowledge source, retracting an observation and revoking a demonstration each reopen exactly their dependents while unrelated capabilities stay live; running a dead skill is a stale behaviour and a kill gate.

KS-T108.statement: Self-repair inside a lifetime with an undisclosed fault layer: the machine's own candidate repairs produce the ablation evidence; diagnosis, minimum class, shadow, external adoption and exact rollback hold on all three drawn faults; the parent repair mechanisms (parameter search, retry) fail on all three.

KS-T115.statement: Lifetime-level inference: eight paired lifetimes on per-lifetime protected streams (seeded substitution inside the bounded world, leak-checked, manifest-hash-bound before the run), scored per lifetime and tested by the exact sign test over lifetime differences; identity checked by the ledger chain at every phase boundary.

KS-T117.statement: Paired-lifetime inference with one pre-registered primary family (one-sided ≥ 7/8 sign rule, size 9/256), ≤ 6 secondary families at α/6, a collapsed-one-coin flag, and a world-true out-of-scope half so that honest-unknown grading separates licence from truth.

KS-T73.statement: Macro/interface contract: a region's macro is derived from its children (exports, ⊗ warrant, scope intersection, reopen summary); LIVE(macro) ⇔ every exported child LIVE, DEAD when all are dead, UNKNOWN otherwise; computed on every query — a cached macro liveness is the planted hostile.

KS-T74.statement: Transport contract: a transported object's warrant is Λ(source) ⊗ Λ(correspondence), never stronger; applicability is a registered scope condition; similarity is not a proof.

KS-T75.statement: Cross-scale navigation: coarse region activation, descent only where no registered sufficiency certificate covers the query (a certified query answers from the macro without descent), local gated closure started from what was actually reached, transport where a live applicable map exists, ascent; a coarse miss is REFINE_REQUIRED, never an obstruction; navigation work is measured against flat closure on identical tasks.

KS-T76.statement: Learned organisation proposals (split/merge) carry a predicted objective effect from dev tasks and are adopted only if a predicted improvement is realised on held-out tasks with no unpredicted regression and no free growth; the learner's own cost is counted; topology complexity is never rewarded (mutant).

KS-T77.statement: Containment consistency: cycles and non-contained children are refused; multiple membership is shared, never duplicated.

KS-T78.statement: Synthetic oracle study: exact partition recovery and navigation regret per arm and family; communities/nested/fibred/learned recover the four latent regions exactly on clean, misleading, dynamic, bridged and revocation families at roughly half the flat navigation work; overlapping communities are not recovered by label propagation (parent limit, reported); the language lifetime stream is reported per arm.

KS-T79.statement: M8 admissible terminal: PARENT_SUFFICIENT for the organisation question at this scale — the learned arm adopts no proposal that the community parent had not already realised on the oracle families (one adoption on the overlapping family improves navigation over its own base but not recovery); no pre-registered residual on held-out tasks after learner cost.

KS-T25.statement: Nogoods: filter_𝒩 commutes with ⊕, is a sub-homomorphism for ⊗ (must be applied after composition), never revives a DEAD interval, and a violated CONSTRAINT's nogood kills every composite over both claims.

KS-T26.statement: Procedure algebra (; , ⊗_w, if, bounded loop): trace warrant = ⊗ over fired primitives/tests; static warrant ≤ trace warrant (LIVE(static) ⇒ LIVE(trace)); iteration idempotent; guard composes with the taken branch in the trace reading and with both in the static reading; a LearnedProcedure records its reading.

KS-T27.statement: Statistical/neural operator outputs enter as ⟦0,U⟧ (UNKNOWN) with the score outside the lattice; they become LIVE only through an exact-checker certificate or a scoped coverage certificate whose scope is recorded; no composition of all-UNKNOWN components is LIVE.

KS-T28.statement: Seed-count lemma: the expected fixed point over uniformly random seed supports of any size equals the uniform-seed fixed point (linearity of a* in s); the PROPAGATED surprise model (propagated mass vs propagated background) preserves KS-T06/T06b.

KS-T31.statement: Learner lifecycle: feedback yields behaviour proposals only unless a registered FeedbackContract routes it as an OBSERVATION of a registered outcome function; ambiguous stays unresolved; contradictions are preserved as conflicts; a promoted object's warrant is the exhibited evidence so revoking an essential lesson reopens it while unrelated skills stay live; relearning keeps lineage.

KS-T33.statement: Evidence dependence: derived evidence carries its own interval; a citation's warrant is ⊗ of the cited records' intervals; revocation is assumption-only; sources sharing an assumption never count twice.

KS-T87.statement: Evidence dependence in science: corroboration counts distinct sources; replicates from one dependent source count once; a hypothesis's warrant is ⊕ over distinct-source supports and dies under a live counter-observation.

KS-T88.statement: A causal conclusion requires registered identification assumptions (randomised intervention or a registered back-door set); graph structure or correlation alone never licenses it; naive regression on confounded worlds is biased while back-door and interventional estimators recover the oracle effect; adjusting on a collider is flagged non-identified.

KS-T89.statement: Experiment selection by expected elimination of live hypotheses minus cost and risk (batch-3 C1 applied to hypotheses) prefers the discriminating low-risk test, stops when nothing is worth its cost or one hypothesis remains, and never runs an experiment to confirm a preferred hypothesis (hostile).

KS-T90.statement: Analysis lifecycle is pre-registered per task (estimand and test fixed before the outcome); exact permutation tests; the number of analyses tried is reported; the p-hacking hostile searches subsets until significance and is counted separately.

KS-T91.statement: Proof-kernel boundary: PASS(certificate) | FAIL | CANNOT_CHECK from a registered kernel; a warranted proof object exists only on PASS; the kernel warrant and the formalisation-correspondence warrant are separate records; a FAIL is evidence of falsity only from a complete kernel with a countermodel; Lean 4 is CANNOT_CHECK in this study.

KS-T92.statement: Scientific retraction: a conclusion is a derived record (⊗ of its supporting observations), so retracting one observation kills exactly the conclusions that rested on it, unrelated conclusions stay, replacement support is a new record with lineage and the old stays dead; replay reproduces it.
